_note: How the fidelity gate ARRIVES at a screen. One entry per in-scope screen
id: which door, which route, and which login gets there. Extending the
gate to another journey is adding entries here — never editing the gate.
arrive: 'anon' (no login), 'worker' (#login-grace), 'field' ([data-login]),
'console:<persona-key>' (the console's persona card, by data-persona), or
'flow:<name>' — a scripted-flow arrival (#179): the gate drives the real
flow first (real POSTs, a unique organisation per arrival) and lands on
the route with the session state the screen holds per-session. Depths:
flow:onboarding (registered), flow:onboarding-terms (registered, with a
second published set so the terms catalogue has 'other sets'),
flow:onboarding-invited (registered + a project's real invitation),
flow:onboarding-terms-request (terms requested, on the checks step),
flow:onboarding-approved (submitted + the operator's real decision),
flow:onboarding-project (approved + invitation accepted, grant minted),
flow:onboarding-wider-request (approved + wider set published + request
opened), flow:onboarding-wider-submitted (documents declared + submitted),
flow:admissions-queue (registered, then signed in as the instance
administrator — the operator's side of the same registration),
flow:admissions-review (as admissions-queue, landing on the registered
organisation's own #/admissions/:pid detail; the route is per-run, so the
map's route stays '' and the flow lands the page itself).
route: the hash route inside the door, or '' for the door's entry screen.
A screen with no entry here is out of the gate's scope and is reported as
such — the gate never silently passes a screen it did not visit.

scope.why: Phase 1 is scoped to J3 — setting up a project (P-1 Org Admin, P-2 Project Configurator) — plus the five connective-tissue screens our own design adds (docs/design/j3-connective-tissue/README.md). The G-2 wave adds the org onboarding journey (g2_1..g2_13; g2_2/g2_3 do not exist in the reference): the onboarding door is deliberately reachable with no persona (#20, #155 phase D) — g2_1 arrives anon, and every screen past it arrives by a flow: mode (#179), because the flow's state is session-scoped by design and only driving the real flow can honestly put a screen in the state its spec draws. The G-1 wave (#187) adds the instance walk (g1_1..g1_6, console:instance — the screens read instance state, so a cold load is honest) and the operator's admission review (g4_1..g4_3, flow:admissions-* — the queue needs a real pending registration, so the arrival registers one first). The rest of the g4 journey (g4_4..g4_7) stays out of the declared scope: g4_6 is a custodian-console screen an earlier wave built to its own rail, and holding it to the reference's G-4 rail is its own piece of work, not this close-out's. Screens the ledger does not call implemented skip with the ledger's own gap note.

g1_1.note: the stand-up front door reads GET /v1/instance — deployment state, no session, so a cold load is the honest arrival

g1_5.note: ledger says compressed (design finding #185: no instance-level invitation primitive), so the gate skips with that note

g4_1.note: #/admissions — the queue must have a real pending row, so the arrival registers an organisation first, signs in as the instance administrator, and lands the page itself (the console token is in-memory, so the gate's post-flow reload would sign the reviewer out)

g4_2.note: #/admissions/:pid — the pid is the arrival's own registration, so the flow lands the page itself

g4_3.note: same detail screen as g4_2: the approve step is the pending registration's decision card

g2_4.note: the decided registration, read back: state, exact terms version, decider

g2_5.note: the org's real (empty) invitation inbox, read back — 'stands alone' is true of a fresh registration

g2_6.note: held permissions vs other published sets, read live; the request door opens only after approval, so the arrival sits after the operator's decision

g2_7.note: declared {kind, ref, hash} references via PUT .../documents, never an upload; needs the open request the wider screen minted

g2_8.note: the submitted request read whole; Withdraw is POST .../withdraw

g2_9.note: inbox from GET .../invitations with a real offer waiting — the seeded project sends it through the real endpoint

g2_10.note: the accepted invitation and the grant the acceptance minted, read back

g2_11.note: the published-terms catalogue for the session's application; a second set is published so 'other sets you could ask for' has something true to say

g2_12.note: checks are recorded verdicts with named owners from GET .../terms-requests/{id}, no fake automation; honestly empty on a fresh application

g2_13.note: the approved terminal state of the same status screen as g2_4
